questions.prompt: When are dual turns permitted at an intersection?
questions.explanation: Two lanes may turn at the same time only where pavement markings or signs show that dual turns are allowed. Key words: "dual turns".

choices.text: Only when turning from a one-way road onto a one-way road
Any time there are at least 2 lanes on the road being entered
Only when indicated by pavement markings or traffic control signs
Only when the road has 6 or more lanes

questions.prompt: Unless otherwise permitted, what lane must a driver be in to turn left from a one-way road?
questions.explanation: To turn left from a one-way road, start from the lane nearest the left curb, unless signs or pavement markings allow another lane.

choices.text: The centre lane
The lane closest to the right curb
The left lane nearest the left curb
The lane to the right of centre

questions.prompt: At a stop sign, a driver must:
questions.explanation: Stop before the stop line or the marked crosswalk. If there is neither, stop before entering the intersection at a point where you can see approaching traffic.

choices.text: Stop in a position where the visibility is the greatest
Stop 10 metres before a marked crosswalk or stop line
Stop in the marked crosswalk or on the stop line
Stop before entering a marked crosswalk or crossing a stop line

questions.prompt: An "uncontrolled intersection":
questions.explanation: An uncontrolled intersection has no traffic lights or signs. Slow down, be ready to stop, and yield to the vehicle on your right.

choices.text: Has a flashing yellow light for one direction of traffic and a flashing red light for the other direction of traffic
Has traffic signs but no traffic control signal lights
Has no traffic control signal lights or traffic signs
Has Yield signs but no Stop signs

questions.prompt: U-turns in urban areas are not permitted at:
questions.explanation: In urban areas, U-turns are not allowed at intersections controlled by traffic lights unless a sign allows them. They are also not allowed between intersections or at alleys. Key words: "urban areas", "not".

choices.text: An intersection with marked traffic lanes
Roads with a landscaped median
An intersection controlled by a traffic control signal
An intersection controlled by Stop signs

questions.prompt: A driver attempting to turn left at a steady green traffic light:
questions.explanation: A steady green light does not give a left-turning driver the right-of-way. Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, and turn only when it is safe.

choices.text: Has the right-of-way over oncoming traffic
Must stop before the pedestrian crosswalk line, then proceed
Has the right-of-way over pedestrians
Must not cross the path of an approaching vehicle unless it is safe

questions.prompt: When turning left from a two-way road onto a one-way road, what lane should the vehicle enter?
questions.explanation: When turning left onto a one-way road, enter the lane nearest the left curb. Key words: "onto a one-way road", "left side".

choices.text: The lane immediately to the right of centre
The lane nearest the curb on the left side of the one-way road
The centre lane of the one-way road
The right lane of the one-way road

questions.prompt: A driver entering a traffic circle:
questions.explanation: Vehicles already in a traffic circle have the right-of-way. When entering, yield to them and wait for a safe gap. Key words: "entering".

choices.text: Must yield to traffic on the right
Must yield to vehicles in the traffic circle
Has the right-of-way

questions.prompt: A vehicle exiting a parking lot onto a roadway:
questions.explanation: When leaving a parking lot, alley or driveway, come to a complete stop before the sidewalk area, then yield to pedestrians and to traffic on the road.

choices.text: Must stop only if there is a Stop sign
Is not required to stop
Must stop before crossing the sidewalk only if there are pedestrians present
Must come to a complete stop

questions.prompt: When approaching a Yield sign, you must:
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down and be ready to stop. Give the right-of-way to traffic that does not face the sign and to all pedestrians, and go only when it is safe.

choices.text: Yield the right-of-way to traffic not facing the sign and all pedestrians in the intersection
Always sound the horn to warn other traffic within the intersection
Expect all other vehicles to yield the right-of-way to you
Come to a stop and proceed after looking to the right and left

questions.prompt: When two vehicles approach an uncontrolled "T" intersection at right angles to each other at approximately the same time:
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, including a "T" intersection, the vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right. Key words: "left".

choices.text: The vehicle on the left must yield the right-of-way
The vehicle on the left has the right-of-way
The vehicle going straight through always has the right-of-way
Both vehicles must stop

questions.prompt: Which statements best describes the steps for turning right at a red traffic light?
questions.explanation: Signal, stop completely, check for traffic and pedestrians,. Yield right-of-way, and then proceed safely, unless a sign prohibits it.

choices.text: Right turns on a red traffic light are never permitted
Signal and make sure there is no sign prohibiting the turn, stop, look left and right, yield the right-of-way, then proceed
Reduce speed before the turn, look right for cyclists, signal and proceed
Signal and reduce speed before the turn, look left, yield to vehicles and proceed

questions.prompt: At a stop sign with no stop line and no marked crosswalk, where must you stop?
questions.explanation: If there is no stop line or marked crosswalk, stop within three metres of the intersecting roadway, where you won't interfere with pedestrians. (Driver's Guide p. 59)

choices.text: Within 3 metres of the intersecting roadway
Within 10 metres of the intersecting roadway
At the edge of the intersecting roadway, wherever you can see best
Within 15 metres of the stop sign

questions.prompt: At a four-way stop, which vehicle should go first?
questions.explanation: At three- and four-way stops, courtesy is to let the vehicle that arrived first go first. (Driver's Guide p. 59)

choices.text: The vehicle going straight
The largest vehicle
The vehicle that arrived first
The vehicle on the left

questions.prompt: Two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time. Which one should go first?
questions.explanation: If two vehicles arrive at the same time, courtesy allows the vehicle on the right to go first. (Driver's Guide p. 59)

choices.text: The vehicle on the left
The vehicle turning left
The faster vehicle
The vehicle on the right

questions.prompt: You approach a yield sign and there are no pedestrians or vehicles you need to yield to. You may:
questions.explanation: If no one needs you to yield, you may go through without coming to a complete stop. Approach at a speed that lets you stop easily. (Driver's Guide p. 59)

choices.text: Come to a complete stop before proceeding
Proceed only after sounding your horn
Wait for a green light
Proceed without coming to a complete stop

questions.prompt: At an intersection with no signs or traffic lights, you must yield to:
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, you must yield the right-of-way to a vehicle on your right. (Driver's Guide p. 59)

choices.text: A vehicle approaching on your left
The vehicle going faster
A vehicle approaching on your right
No one; the first vehicle into the intersection has the right-of-way

questions.prompt: You have the right-of-way, but another driver does not seem to be yielding. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Even if you have the right-of-way, you are still responsible for doing everything you can to prevent a collision. (Driver's Guide p. 58)

choices.text: Proceed, since the law is on your side
Sound your horn and continue
Do everything you can to avoid a collision, even if it means giving up the right-of-way
Speed up to get through first

questions.prompt: A police officer directing traffic signals you to go through a red light. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Directions given by a peace officer or police officer must be followed over traffic signs or signals. (Driver's Guide p. 58)

choices.text: Follow the officer's directions
Wait for the light to turn green
Stop and ask the officer to confirm
Turn right instead

questions.prompt: The light is green, but traffic is backed up on the other side of the intersection. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Don't enter an intersection until you can clear it completely, including the crosswalk on the other side. (Driver's Guide p. 60)

choices.text: Enter the intersection, since your light is green
Enter the intersection and stop in the crosswalk
Wait behind the intersection until there is room to clear it completely
Change lanes to go around the traffic

questions.prompt: In which direction does traffic flow around a roundabout or traffic circle?
questions.explanation: Traffic always circulates counterclockwise around the centre island. (Driver's Guide p. 61)

choices.text: Clockwise
Either direction, depending on your exit
Counterclockwise
The direction shown by the first sign only

questions.prompt: In a single-lane roundabout, when should you turn on your right signal if you are not taking the first exit?
questions.explanation: Turn on your right signal after you pass the exit before the one you intend to use. (Driver's Guide pp. 61–62)

choices.text: As you enter the roundabout
After passing the exit before the one you want
Only after you have left the roundabout
You don't need to signal in a roundabout

questions.prompt: In a two-lane roundabout, which lane should you use if you plan to go past the first exit?
questions.explanation: Drivers planning to travel past the first exit should enter, stay in, and exit from the left lane. The right lane is for the first exit. (Driver's Guide pp. 62–63)

choices.text: The right lane
Either lane, changing lanes as needed
The right lane, then move left inside the circle
The left lane

questions.prompt: Inside a two-lane roundabout, who must yield?
questions.explanation: While in the circle, drivers in the right lane must yield to drivers in the left lane. Don't change lanes in the circle. (Driver's Guide p. 62)

choices.text: Drivers in the left lane yield to drivers in the right lane
Drivers in the right lane yield to drivers in the left lane
No one; both lanes have equal right-of-way
Drivers who entered last yield to everyone

questions.prompt: In a roundabout, you realize you can't exit safely at your intended exit. What should you do?
questions.explanation: If you can't stop or exit safely, stay in your lane and go around the roundabout again. (Driver's Guide p. 63)

choices.text: Stop in the roundabout until it is safe to exit
Cut across the other lane to exit
Stay in your lane and go around again
Reverse back to the exit

questions.prompt: When making a right turn, how close to the curb or edge of the road should you stay?
questions.explanation: Stay centred in the turning lane, not more than one metre from the curb or road's edge, as you approach, turn, and leave the intersection. (Driver's Guide p. 64)

choices.text: Within 3 metres
In the centre of the road
Within 1 metre
As far from the curb as possible

questions.prompt: You should be in the correct lane for a turn at least how far before the intersection?
questions.explanation: Be in your proper turning lane at least 15 metres (50 feet) before the intersection. (Driver's Guide pp. 63, 65)

choices.text: 5 metres
50 metres
15 metres
100 metres

questions.prompt: You are waiting in the intersection to turn left. How should your front wheels be pointed?
questions.explanation: Keep your front wheels pointed straight ahead, so that if you are hit from behind you won't be pushed into oncoming traffic. (Driver's Guide p. 65)

choices.text: Turned to the left, ready for the turn
Turned to the right
It doesn't matter while you are stopped
Straight ahead

questions.prompt: When turning left from a two-way road onto another two-way road, which lane should you turn into?
questions.explanation: Turn from the lane nearest and to the right of the yellow line, into the lane nearest and to the right of the yellow line. (Driver's Guide p. 65)

choices.text: The curb lane on the far side
Any lane that is clear
The lane nearest and to the right of the yellow line
The lane to the left of the yellow line

questions.prompt: When turning left from a one-way road onto a two-way road, which lane should you turn from?
questions.explanation: Turn from the lane nearest the left side of the road, into the lane nearest to the right of the yellow line. (Driver's Guide p. 66)

choices.text: The lane nearest the left side of the one-way road
The lane nearest the right side of the one-way road
The centre lane
Any lane, as long as you signal

questions.prompt: You are turning right, and a vehicle is parked close to the corner in the curb lane of the road you are entering. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Turn into the first available lane to the left of the parked vehicle. Yield to vehicles approaching from your left in that lane. (Driver's Guide p. 64)

choices.text: Turn into the curb lane and stop behind the parked vehicle
Wait until the parked vehicle leaves
Turn into the first available lane to the left of the parked vehicle
Turn wide into the far lane

questions.prompt: Before turning left off a two-lane highway, why should you shoulder check to the left?
questions.explanation: Do a shoulder check to the left to be sure you are not being passed by another vehicle on your left. (Driver's Guide p. 65)

choices.text: To make sure no vehicle is passing you on the left
To check for pedestrians on the right
To look for a police vehicle
To see the road you are turning onto

questions.prompt: Outside urban areas, U-turns are not permitted:
questions.explanation: In rural areas, U-turns are not permitted on a curve, or on an approach to or near the crest of a hill where drivers within 150 metres can't see you. (Driver's Guide p. 67)

choices.text: On any highway
Between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.
Anywhere there is a broken centre line
On a curve or near the crest of a hill where other drivers within 150 metres can't see you

questions.prompt: Do right-of-way rules apply at intersections inside parking lots?
questions.explanation: Parking lots have intersections without signs or signals, and the right-of-way rules apply. (Driver's Guide p. 60)

choices.text: No, parking lots are private property
Yes, the same rules as uncontrolled intersections apply
Only if there are painted lines
Only during business hours
